review_candidates.title: Product Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Job Title: Product Coordinator Monthly Pay: $3,721 - $5,558 USD per month Summary: Accurate product updates, clear ownership, and complete handoffs are the standards that define good work in this role. The Product Coordinator organizes product coordination activities within the product management team, working under a product manager to keep approved priorities moving toward completion. The position works with product managers, customer support colleagues, sales contacts, and operations partners to connect requests, decisions, and launch preparations. This fully remote position offers work from home in Texas, United States, with desk-based responsibilities focused on organized information and dependable follow-through. The role requires a 40-hour weekly commitment. Working days and shift times may vary. Job Responsibilities: • Receive product requests through a shared queue, emails, and planning meetings; organize each item so the product manager can review its purpose and urgency. • Check incoming requests for a clear description, intended audience, requested timing, and supporting context; ask the submitting colleague to clarify missing information before review. • Enter approved activities, owners, target dates, and dependencies in a project management tool such as Asana, keeping task details aligned with product manager decisions. • Maintain product trackers using a spreadsheets and data entry tool such as Google Sheets, checking that milestones, statuses, and references match the current plan. • Organize product review meetings, circulate discussion points, capture decisions, and distribute action summaries that identify responsible colleagues and expected next steps after each discussion. • Coordinate launch readiness checklists with customer support, sales, and operations contacts, confirming that approved product information and internal preparation tasks are ready for handoff. • Follow up with task owners when updates are missing or dates approach, and flag unresolved dependencies or conflicting priorities to the product manager. • Compare product summaries and launch trackers against approved source information, asking the relevant owner to resolve discrepancies before updates reach other teams. • Prepare concise progress summaries covering completed activities, outstanding questions, upcoming milestones, and decisions needed, without changing product priorities or making commitments independently. • Close completed coordination items after owner confirmation; quality is judged by accuracy, turnaround, complete notes, dependable follow-up, and clear handoffs throughout the workflow. Qualifications: • High school diploma or equivalent. • About 1-2 years of product coordination, product team support, or related administrative experience preferred. • Familiarity with product development stages, launch preparation, and the distinction between coordinating activities and setting product direction. • Working knowledge of task trackers, shared spreadsheets, status updates, and methods for keeping information consistent across related activities. • Understanding of requirements management and dependency management sufficient to identify missing context and route questions to the appropriate owner. • Clear written and verbal communication for requesting updates, summarizing decisions, and explaining outstanding actions to different internal audiences. • Ability to compare information carefully, organize competing requests, and recognize when a decision needs product manager guidance. • A reliable computer, high-speed internet, and quiet private workspace; availability for the 40-hour weekly commitment and agreed working days and shift times. • Authorization to work in the United States. Perks & Benefits: • Fully remote work with desk-based product coordination responsibilities and ongoing connection to the product management team. • Structured onboarding and training on the named systems, product trackers, handoff practices, and internal coordination procedures. • Regular check-ins with the team lead to review priorities, discuss questions, and receive feedback on work quality. • Opportunities to build product launch coordination, requirements management, dependency management, and cross-team communication skills through everyday responsibilities. • Health coverage, paid leave, a 401(k), maternity leave, and stipends.

review_candidates.title: Hebrew First Language Teacher
review_candidates.description: St Andrews International School Bangkok is one of 88 schools in the Nord Anglia Education (NAE) family. We offer a British educational curriculum with an international perspective that begins in Nursery and leads up to IGCSE examinations in Year 11, and culminates with the International Baccalaureate Diploma after completing Year 13. We are an inclusive school that invites children from all backgrounds and abilities to participate in the educational offerings on our diverse campus. Founded in 1997 on an attractive, conveniently located site, with excellent facilities and access to local transportation. Today we have more than 2,400 students over a Primary School and High School campus, representing some 68 nationalities ranging from Foundation Stage to Year 13. Our state-of-the-art High School campus (next to Ekkamai BTS) opened in August 2017 giving our students the benefit of world-class teaching and facilities. As part of the NAE family of schools, we are delighted to be able to offer some unique collaborations with world-class establishments, including the Juilliard School of Performing Arts, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), and UNICEF. About The Role At St Andrews, Hebrew is taught as a First Language (native) programme, and we are seeking an enthusiastic and experienced Hebrew specialist teacher to join our Languages team. The successful candidate will have experience teaching Hebrew as a native language to Primary and High School students and will play an important role in the development and introduction of a new Hebrew First Language programme at St Andrews. The successful candidate will teach Hebrew First Language to native-speaking students from Year 1 to Year 9. Class sizes are small and students are motivated and enthusiastic, enjoying a lively and engaging approach to learning through a wide range of teaching and learning techniques. The ideal candidate will convey a genuine enthusiasm for the subject and work collaboratively with colleagues to establish and develop a strong, engaging and progressive Hebrew curriculum across Year 1 to Year 9. As this is a new programme, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to its development from the outset. This will include supporting the planning and implementation of the Hebrew First Language curriculum, developing appropriate schemes of work and resources, establishing progression across year groups, and helping to ensure that the programme meets the needs of native Hebrew-speaking students at different stages of their learning. The ideal candidate will have extensive subject knowledge and experience teaching Hebrew using appropriate first-language teaching approaches to native-speaking Primary and High School students. Previous experience teaching Hebrew First Language across multiple Key Stages, particularly from Year 1 to Year 9, is essential. Experience in developing or introducing a new language programme or curriculum would be a significant advantage. The successful candidate may also be required to support the wider Languages team and contribute to the development of language learning across the school. All Languages classrooms have interactive whiteboards and access to the internet, and there is a strong commitment to integrating the teaching and use of ICT skills into all areas of the curriculum, where appropriate, with iPads. As well as their teaching, all teachers are also expected to contribute positively to both the school’s pastoral systems and the extra-curricular programme, offering an Extra-Curricular Activity that either supports or extends the students’ learning in their subject area, or from another area of personal interest. About The School At St Andrews, we pride ourselves on being an inclusive school, and we have an excellent reputation for supporting children with special educational needs. Experience of teaching children with dyslexia, mild autism, ADHD etc. would be very good prior experience for a teacher wishing to join our team. Our Mission Statement commits us to meeting ‘all the needs of the individual learner’, and this applies equally to those students targeting the very highest grades at IGCSE and IB. Our Community Joining St Andrews means becoming part of a warm and inclusive community, where teachers contribute beyond the classroom. In addition to teaching, you’ll engage in our vibrant pastoral system, residential trips, and offer extracurricular activities that enhance student growth, whether in academics, creative arts, sports, or social initiatives. Curriculum and Learning Approach Our curriculum broadly follows the English National Curriculum with an inclusive, international perspective. Senior students take IGCSEs and the IB Diploma, with options for the IB Career-Related Pathway and International BTECs, catering to our diverse community. We embrace technology, adapting to the continuous changes, ensuring staff and students have the tools for digital learning. Every teacher receives a personal device. Safeguarding At St Andrews St Andrews is committed to ensuring the safety of all our students, and expects all staff to share the same commitment (see our Child Protection Code of Conduct). No teacher will be appointed without at least two references, including one from the most recent employer, a ten year criminal record check and relevant regional Prohibition Order/DBS checks. Application Process If you would like to apply for a position at our school, please complete the application process through Jobtrain, accessible via the Nord Anglia Education website: http://www.nordangliaeducation.com/careers/ The closing date for applications is 18th September 2026 , with applications being reviewed as they are received. Please email recruitment@standrews.ac.th if you require any further information. At Nord Anglia Education we are committed to providing a world class, safe, happy environment in which children and young people can thrive and learn. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all our pupils where we embrace all race, abilities, religions, genders, and cultures. All post holders in regulated activity (having regular unsupervised contact with children) are subject to appropriate national and international vetting procedures including satisfactory criminal record checks from both your country of residence/birth and any country of residence within the last 10 years. We welcome applications from suitable qualified persons from all diverse backgrounds Please note, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
